headline: Approved January minutes, accepted treasurer and superintendent reports, and discussed future cemetery expansion limits.
summary: The Board reviewed the Treasurer's report showing $11,376.38 in Perpetual Care income for January and the Superintendent's report listing six burials for the month. Members discussed that the cemetery is running low on space and talked about limited options for future expansion, with more discussion planned for a later meeting.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the January 21, 2026 meeting as read; all in favor.
Accepted the Treasurer's Trust Report as read; all in favor.
Accepted the Superintendent's report as read; all in favor.
plain_text:
MEETING MINUTES OF: February 18, 2026
A meeting of the Cemetery Board of Trustees was held at the Forest Dale Cemetery, 150 Forest Street, Malden on 
the above date, in accordance with the Notice of Meeting, as provided in G.L. c.30A,§§ 18-25. Notice was filed with 
the City Clerk’s Office, City of Malden.
President James Tuxbury called the meeting to order at 5:00 P.M. Members present were James Tuxbury, Vincent 
Miraglia, Joseph Barriss, Sheila Fermano and Superintendent Chris Rosa.
APPROVAL OF MINUTES: The minutes of the January 21, 2026 meeting were read and upon the motion of 
Vincent Miraglia and seconded by Joseph Barriss, the Board voted to accept the minutes as read; all were in 
CARRIED
CORRESPONDENCE: None
TREASURER REPORT: Cemetery Superintendent Chris Rosa provided the following information: The Cemetery 
Trust received income for the month of January the amount of $11,376.38 for Perpetual Care. This money was 
turned over to the Treasurer’s office to be added to the Cemetery Trust accounts. Upon the motion of Joseph 
Barriss and seconded by Vincent Miraglis, the Board voted to accept the Trust Report as read; all were in favor. 
CARRIED
SUPERINTENDENT’S REPORT: The Superintendent’s report was received by the Trustees. Superintendent Rosa 
provided the following information: burials for the month of January were four (4) full burials in existing lots; one (1) 
double deep full burial; and one Veteran (1) burial for a total of six (6) burials.
 Superintendent Rosa said February was a busy month for burials in spite of the snow, but general 
cemetery maintenance obviously could not be addressed due to the unescapable weather.
 The Superintendent also informed the Trustees that the cemetery is quickly running out of space, and he
had concerns about the near future with regard to expansion plans.
The motion to accept Superintendent’s report was made by Sheila Fermano and seconded by Vincent Miraglia; all 
were in favor. CARRIED
OLD BUSINESS/GENERAL CEMETERY BUSINESS: Discussion on possible future expansion in the Cemetery, 
but potential would be very limited. Further discussion at a future meeting.
Next meeting of the Board of Trustees: The next meeting of the Cemetery Board of Trustees will be held on 
Wednesday, March 18, 2026.
ADJOURMENT: All business before the Board of Trustees having been completed and upon motion of Joseph 
Barriss and seconded by Vinnie Miraglia, the meeting was adjourned at 5:45 P.M.
Respectfully submitted,
Sheila Fermano, Secretary
James Tuxbury, President
Sheila L. Fermano, Secretary
Joseph Barris, Trustee
Vincent Miraglia, Trustee
